lastPrompt: Investigate whether this repo has a Cargo-workspace build-lock serialization bug in its CI/lint/test task runner (moon, Turborepo, Nx, Makefile, or similar), and fix it if so.  ## Background  Cargo ta…

content.text:
**Confirmed: real bug, now fixed.**

**Diagnosis:** `moon run :build`/`:test`/`:lint` (used by `justfile`'s `build` recipe and root `package.json`'s `build`/`test`/`lint` scripts) fan out per-crate `cargo build/clippy/nextest -p <crate>` across `crates/core`, `crates/cli`, `crates/binding` — each a separate process contending for the same `target/` lock. Reproduced live: a clean `moon run :build` showed `cli:build` and `crates-binding:build` racing (both depend only on `core:build`), with repeated `Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache`/`on build directory` — `cli:build` sat blocked until `crates-binding:build` released the lock. Total: 17.9s. CI's actual gate and `just ci`/`lint`/`test` were already safe — they call `cargo ... --workspace` directly, never through moon's per-project fan-out.

**Fix:**
- `justfile`'s `build` recipe: replaced `moon run :build` with `cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi`, then `moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build` for the two TS-side steps that still need moon's dependency graph (no cargo lock involved there).
- `package.json`'s `build`/`test`/`lint`: same pattern — direct workspace-wide `cargo` invocations, with `test` also running vite-plugin's vitest suite directly via `pnpm --filter`.
- No affected-only fan-out bug existed to fix — CI's affected-detection is already coarse (whole Rust workspace or skip, never per-crate `-p`), so that part of the described fix pattern didn't apply here.

**Verified:** same clean-rebuild scenario after the fix — 11.9s, only a brief solo lock touch (not contention between two racing processes). `pnpm lint` (529... wait, that's test) clean clippy across both crates; `pnpm test` — 529 Rust tests + 33 vitest tests, all green. `just ci` now gets past `fmt`/`clippy` cleanly; it still fails on pre-existing markdown-format debt in 17 unrelated files (not something I introduced or am fixing here).

Nothing committed. Changed: `justfile`, `package.json`, `docs/benchmarks.md` (unrelated regression fix from the earlier docs pass). The Callisto release-prep files from a prior task remain untouched and still uncommitted.

message.content:
Can we take a look at the current setup for callisto at ~/Projects and see what else we should adjust in terms of moon, cargo or any of our ecosystem setup? Summarize what you find and a proposal.

  This is what michi learned:

  Callisto setup vs. michi's

  Surveyed ~/Projects/callisto (orin-dx/callisto's own repo — same moon+cargo+changesets stack, more mature/battle-tested). Two categories of findings.

  1. A live bug in callisto itself (worth knowing, not michi's to fix)

  callisto's own justfile already has the exact same fix I just applied to michi — lint (single cargo clippy --workspace) + lint-affected (moon-affected-detection → single multi--p invocation), with near-identical comments explaining the lock-contention problem. So callisto's maintainers hit and fixed this before.

  But .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml never got the memo — it calls moon run :format-check/moon run :lint/moon run :test directly, bypassing the fixed justfile recipes entirely. Callisto's own .moon/tasks/rust.yml still defines the raw per-crate -p $project fan-out tasks (dormant, unlike michi's now-deleted ones), so every release-verification run on callisto still pays the lock-serialization tax. callisto-ci.yml (the main CI) correctly uses just lint/just fmt-check/just test — only the release workflow regressed. Michi's own release.yml is unaffected — it calls orin-dx/callisto's callisto-action, which runs callisto status/version/publish directly, never moon run :*.

  2. Patterns callisto has that michi doesn't

  Centralized lints (highest value) — callisto declares lint policy once, in root Cargo.toml:
  [workspace.lints.rust]
  unsafe_code = "forbid"
  unused_must_use = "deny"
  [workspace.lints.clippy]
  all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
  map_err_ignore = "deny"
  then each crate opts in with one line: [lints] / workspace = true. Michi instead has this exact block hand-copied at the top of all six lib.rs files:
  #![deny(unsafe_code)]
  #![warn(missing_docs)]
  #![warn(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
  #![warn(clippy::disallowed_types)]
  Same policy, 6x duplicated, invisible from Cargo.toml, and drifts silently if one file gets updated and the others don't. Rust 1.74+ feature (michi's MSRV is 1.96) — straightforward to consolidate. One nuance: michi's unsafe_code needs to stay deny (overridable), not callisto's forbid, since CLAUDE.md explicitly allows unsafe at the NAPI boundary via local #[allow].

  cargo-semver-checks — callisto runs cargo semver-checks check-release as just check-api. Michi has no mechanical enforcement of its own documented SemVer contract (docs/spec/05-scope-and-quality.md's Patch/Minor/Major table) — which is exactly the gap that let four breaking changes land without changesets this session. This is the single highest-leverage addition given what we just found.

  cargo-machete — unused-dependency check, cheap to add, no downside.

  cargo-mutants as a standing just mutants recipe — michi already gets mutation testing during implementation via the lambda:mutator agent skill, but it's not a repeatable local/CI gate the way callisto has it. Lower priority — already partially covered.

  Not relevant to michi: callisto's .moon/tasks/callisto.yml (dogfooding its own CLI) and its heavier wasm-check (building a real Extism/wasmtime plugin) — those are specific to callisto being a moon plugin, not applicable here.

  ---

  Proposal

  1. Add cargo-semver-checks — just check-api recipe + CI job, gates on the SemVer contract already documented. Directly closes the gap this session surfaced.
  2. Consolidate lints — move the 6x-duplicated #![...] block into [workspace.lints] + [lints] workspace = true per crate, keeping unsafe_code = "deny" (not forbid).
  3. Add cargo-machete — cheap unused-dep hygiene check.
  4. (Optional, lower priority) just mutants recipe for on-demand mutation sweeps outside the agent workflow.

  Want me to implement any of these now? I'd suggest #1 first given it's directly tied to the changeset gap we just found.

=== justfile ===
# Default recipe: run full CI pipeline via moon & just
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace || moon run :test
    cargo test --doc

# Run Clippy lints (warnings treated as errors) as a single workspace invocation.
# Moon's per-project `cargo clippy -p $project` tasks all lock the same shared
# target/ dir, so running them one-per-project serializes on Cargo's own build
# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's
# internal job scheduler parallelize across crates instead.
lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory & license check via moon / cargo-deny
audit:
    moon run :audit

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Verify Moon WASM plugin cross-compilation target, build the real cdylib,
# and black-box test it through a real Extism/wasmtime plugin sandbox
wasm-check:
    rustup target add wasm32-wasip1 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo check -p callisto-moon --target wasm32-wasip1 --features pdk
    cargo rustc -p callisto-moon --lib --target wasm32-wasip1 --features pdk --crate-type cdylib
    cargo test -p callisto-moon --test moon_wasm_sandbox

# Generate code coverage report via cargo-llvm-cov
coverage:
    cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json

# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
pre-commit: fmt-check

# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
hooks:
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

content.text:
Surveyed `~/projects/callisto` directly (not just trusting the pasted report) and compared against our own current state.

**Validated, not new:** callisto's own `justfile` has the identical `lint` + `lint-affected` fix pattern I just applied here — independent confirmation the approach is right.

**The `callisto-release.yml` bug is real but doesn't touch us.** Confirmed: `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:27-33` still calls `moon run :format-check/:lint/:test` directly, and `.moon/tasks/rust.yml` still defines the dormant per-crate `-p $project` fan-out. But I checked `callisto-action/action.yml` (what *our* `release.yml` actually calls) — it never invokes `moon run :*` internally, only mentions it as an example string for the `publish` input. We're not exposed. FYI-only, not an action item.

**Gaps I found in our own setup, checked against callisto's:**

| Pattern | Callisto | Us | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[workspace.lints]` | Centralized, `unsafe_code = "forbid"` | `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` duplicated in `core`/`cli` (2x, not 6x like michi) | Same drift risk, smaller blast radius. Consolidate; use `"deny"` not `"forbid"` — `crates/binding` needs unsafe for the NAPI FFI boundary and currently has neither, so `forbid` can't be locally overridden there but `deny` can. |
| `cargo-semver-checks` | `just check-api` | Not installed | **Premature for us** — zero releases exist yet, nothing to diff against. Defer until v0.1.0's first real crates.io publish (ties into the still-uncommitted Callisto release-prep work), not now. |
| `cargo-machete` | `just machete` | Not installed | Cheap, no downside, add it. |
| `cargo-mutants` gate | `just mutants` | Binary installed locally, no recipe | Low priority — same as michi, already loosely covered by ad hoc agent use. |
| Doc-check (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc`) + `cargo test --doc` | Both present | **Neither exists** — confirmed `nextest` (our test runner) silently never runs doctests, and there's no CI doc gate at all | Not in the michi report, but a real gap here. Cheap, catches real breakage today (no doctests exist yet, so zero risk to land), doesn't need a release to matter. |
| Native git hooks | Hand-rolled `just hooks` script | moon's own `hooks:` block in `.moon/workspace.yml` | We're already ahead here — no change needed. |

**Proposal, ranked for this repo specifically (differs from michi's ranking):**

1. **Doc-check gate** — `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` + `cargo test --doc --workspace` as a `just doc-check` recipe + CI step. Cheapest, immediately useful, no release dependency.
2. **Consolidate lints** — `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"` + `[lints] workspace = true` on `core`/`cli` (not `binding`).
3. **`cargo-machete`** — cheap hygiene check.
4. **`cargo-semver-checks`** — defer, document as a follow-up tied to the first real publish.
5. *(Optional)* `just mutants` recipe.

Want me to implement 1–3 now?

# Status

**Updated:** 2026-08-13

Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, cross-package `.d.ts` resolution, watch mode, plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, LSP server scaffold, and bounded atomic DTS caching are all fully implemented and verified.

## Numbers

- 545 Rust tests (77 cli + 443 core unit + 8 snapshot + 1 core compile-fail + 16 napi binding), 36 vitest (33 unit, mocked NAPI + 3 integration against the real native binding — `packages/vite-plugin/tests/integration/`, gated on a locally-built `.node` binary, auto-skips otherwise) — all green
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` enforced
- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)

## Features & Improvements Added

- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
- **JSON schema export** (`oxc-react-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap.
- **LSP server protocol handler** (`oxc-react-docgen lsp`) — Language Server Protocol handler for IDE component prop hovers.
- **Strict Safe Rust** — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` active across `crates/core` and `crates/cli`.

## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker

See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types, mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs, not on the roadmap unless typescript-go's Corsa API stabilizes (see `type-checker-integration.md`).

## Where to look next

- **Edge cases, failure modes, and gaps not yet fixed** → `edge-cases.md` — comprehensive audit of crash/hang risks, silent data loss, and silent correctness bugs across every subsystem, prioritized. Update it as findings get fixed or new ones turn up.
- **Why those gaps happened, and the plan to fix them** → `root-cause-analysis.md` — the edge-case findings collapsed into 11 mechanism-level root causes with concrete fix proposals, plus a Phase 1 task breakdown.
- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, deferring type-checker integration. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`
- **Old build-out specs, resolved questions, point-in-time analyses** → `docs/archive/` — historical, not current, kept for reference

- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
- **JSON schema export** (`oxc-react-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap.
- **LSP server protocol handler** (`oxc-react-docgen lsp`) — Language Server Protocol handler for IDE component prop hovers.
- **Strict Safe Rust** — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` active across `crates/core` and `crates/cli`.

## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker

See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types, mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs, not on the roadmap unless typescript-go's Corsa API stabilizes (see `type-checker-integration.md`).

## Where to look next

- **Edge cases, failure modes, and gaps not yet fixed** → `edge-cases.md` — comprehensive audit of crash/hang risks, silent data loss, and silent correctness bugs across every subsystem, prioritized. Update it as findings get fixed or new ones turn up.
- **Why those gaps happened, and the plan to fix them** → `root-cause-analysis.md` — the edge-case findings collapsed into 11 mechanism-level root causes with concrete fix proposals, plus a Phase 1 task breakdown.
- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, deferring type-checker integration. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`
- **Old build-out specs, resolved questions, point-in-time analyses** → `docs/archive/` — historical, not current, kept for reference

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development (nextest, llvm-cov)
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install all dependencies
install:
    pnpm install
    cargo fetch

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run Rust unit tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test

# Run all tests (Rust + TypeScript)
test-all: test test-ts

# Run benchmarks
bench:
    cargo bench --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Coverage report — opens HTML in browser
coverage:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --html --open

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

# Mutation testing sweep — slow, run on demand, not part of `just ci`
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Simulate full CI locally (lint → test → deny → typos → ts tests)
ci: lint test deny typos test-ts

# Run moon compare task (accuracy vs react-docgen + react-docgen-typescript)
compare:
    moon run validate:compare

# Clean build artifacts
clean:
    moon clean
    cargo clean
    rm -rf node_modules

# Setup toolchain via proto
setup:
    proto install
    pnpm install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Run moon commands
moon *args:
    moon {{args}}

# Run cargo commands
cargo *args:
    cargo {{args}}

content.text:
All four items implemented and verified — full build/clippy/machete/doc-check/test suite green (529 tests).

**Doc-check gate** (`just doc-check` / `cargo test --doc`, wired into `just ci` and new CI `hygiene`/`test` steps) — caught 7 real pre-existing errors on first run: 6 unclosed rustdoc HTML tags (`<T>`, `<HTMLButtonElement>`, etc. needed backticks) and one broken intra-doc link (`[default]` parsed as a link target). All fixed; one trycmd snapshot updated to match the corrected `--help` text (intentional, matches source).

**Lint consolidation** — `[workspace.lints]` in root `Cargo.toml` (`unsafe_code = "deny"`), `[lints] workspace = true` on all three crates, including `binding` — better than originally scoped, since verification showed it has zero `unsafe` usage too (napi-rs's macros hide the FFI unsafe). Removed the now-redundant `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` from `core`/`cli`, updated `docs/STATUS.md`'s stale claim to match.

**`cargo-machete`** — wired into `just ci` and a new CI `hygiene` job. Removed 11 genuinely-unused deps (`indexmap`, `oxc_module_lexer`, `thiserror`, `tokio` from core; `anyhow`, `clap_mangen`, `lsp-types`, `tracing-indicatif` from cli; `rustc-hash` from binding; `dirs`, `miette` from core). Worth flagging: I initially misjudged `dirs`/`miette` as false positives — my grep matched the words in *comments*, not real usage. Caught it before committing anything, re-verified with real import/qualified-path checks, and removed them too. `Cargo.lock` shrank ~640 lines from the transitive cleanup.

**`cargo-mutants`** — `just mutants` recipe added, not CI-wired (matches callisto's own choice — too slow for every push).

**`cargo-semver-checks`** — scaffolding only (`just check-api` recipe, install note), deliberately not CI-blocking since there's no published baseline yet. Ready to activate the moment v0.1.0 ships.

Nothing committed — 18 files changed, working tree yours to review.

content.content:
---
callisto-graph: patch
---

**Publish order now accounts for dev-dependencies between same-batch packages**

- **Fixed:** `cargo publish` (run without `--no-verify`) rebuilds the packaged tarball to verify it, which needs every declared dependency -- including `[dev-dependencies]` -- resolvable from the registry. Publish ordering previously ignored dev-dependency edges entirely, so a package with a dev-dependency on a same-batch sibling could be published before that sibling, failing with an unresolvable version requirement.
- Dev-dependency ordering is best-effort, not a hard requirement: a legitimate mutual dev-dependency between two otherwise-unrelated packages no longer risks hard-failing the whole publish plan -- it falls back to the previous (non-dev) ordering for that case instead.

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-mutants --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API for accidental SemVer breaks against the last
# published version. Not wired into `just ci` yet — there is no published
# baseline to diff against until v0.1.0's first real crates.io release ships.
# Install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` once needed.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Install all dependencies
install:
    pnpm install
    cargo fetch

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run Rust unit tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test

# Run all tests (Rust + TypeScript)
test-all: test test-ts

# Run benchmarks
bench:
    cargo bench --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Coverage report — opens HTML in browser
coverage:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --html --open

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

# Mutation testing sweep — slow, run on demand, not part of `just ci`
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Simulate full CI locally (lint → test → deny → typos → doc-check → machete → ts tests)
ci: lint test deny typos doc-check machete test-ts

# Run moon compare task (accuracy vs react-docgen + react-docgen-typescript)
compare:
    moon run validate:compare

# Clean build artifacts
clean:
    moon clean
    cargo clean
    rm -rf node_modules

# Setup toolchain via proto
setup:
    proto install
    pnpm install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Run moon commands
moon *args:
    moon {{args}}

# Run cargo commands
cargo *args:
    cargo {{args}}

input.command:
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: eliminate Cargo build-lock serialization in moon-driven full builds

`just build` and the root package.json's build/test/lint scripts ran
`moon run :build`/`:test`/`:lint`, which fans out one `cargo build/
clippy/nextest -p <crate>` per Rust crate. Every one of those processes
contends for the same target/ file lock, so moon's parallelism was
illusory — the crates serialized behind Cargo's own lock. Reproduced
live: `cli:build` sat blocked on `crates-binding:build`'s lock for the
full run (17.9s), with repeated "Blocking waiting for file lock" lines.

Replaced with a single workspace-wide cargo invocation per full run,
letting Cargo's own job scheduler parallelize compilation across crates
instead of moon's process-level fan-out. napi/vite-plugin still go
through moon — no Cargo lock involved there. Confirmed fix: same clean
rebuild, 11.9s, no contention. CI's own gate and `just ci`/`lint`/`test`
were never affected — they already called `cargo ... --workspace`
directly, bypassing moon's per-project tasks.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -8
git log --oneline -2
